chemicalCorrectness: Main equation is H–O− + Br–CH2–CH2–Br → HO–CH2–CH2–Br + Br−: atoms and total charge −1 are conserved in this single substitution. The green new C–O bond gives oxygen bonds to H and C and leaves the other C–Br intact. No extra H transfer or pentavalent carbon is depicted.

Large blue two-electron arrow clearly originates beside the displayed reacting O lone pair, points toward the left primary carbon and is distinct from the ordinary straight reaction arrow. The short lower blue arrow is anchored immediately below the left C–Br bond and curves toward the departing left Br. Tiny glyph clearance does not create a competing H-origin or wrong-bond interpretation.

The two visible electron dots identify only the reacting pair. No full Lewis shell is claimed: the unshown other lone pairs are not a literal claim that hydroxide has only one lone pair. The visible separate raised minus sign correctly identifies hydroxide.

The lower diol structure HO–CH2–CH2–OH has two OH termini and is explicitly separated and labelled after the second substitution. It does not pretend that the balanced one-step upper reaction already forms the diol.
wholeGoalAndCaseFit: This two-carbon orienting example gives the elementary local mechanism and later bifunctional alcohol idea required by the goal. It differs from the six-carbon and three-carbon supplied assessment cases, preserving genuine transfer demands.

The image does not show both complete electron-pair steps, overall two-step charge balance, molecular-distribution reasoning or monofunctional ethanol comparison; those remain in the full supplied material and are not declared image-based evidence of understanding. It makes no real yield or laboratory preparation claim.
findings.nativeFinding: Correct short structural formulas, electron arrows, charge and distinction between intermediate and subsequent diol. Friendly clear comic diagram; no conflicting ball model, person perspective or instrument scale.

Main title is readable; terse labels are small but identifiable. No mandatory explanatory paragraph must be read to distinguish the two stages. The dot pair and subscripts are small, but discernible rather than merged into a contradictory structure.

findings.altAssessment: Supplied alt text accurately describes the first substitution, bromide and separately subsequent ethane-1,2-diol. No assertion of complete Lewis notation or observed learner execution.

chemicalCorrectness: Separate citric acid and water cards feed the acidic-solution bottle, matching acid component versus aqueous mixture. No concentration, acid strength, molecular mechanism or universal hazard classification is asserted.

Central white glazed ceramic surface has a chalky deposit/clean contrast. The prominent magnifier asks Material geeignet? with Angaben prüfen and Eignung prüfen, preserving dependence on the particular substance/material instructions instead of blanket ceramic/metal permission.

Closed bottle, goggles, information card and two large crossed-out tasting/mixing symbols match the supplied handling context. Nothing shows somebody tasting, applying on skin, freely mixing chemicals or carrying out an unapproved experiment.
Lemon imagery provides familiar context but is counterbalanced by explicit no-tasting and information-dependent handling; it does not identify the closed classroom sample as food or harmless.
wholeGoalAndCaseFit: Shows the intended three related concepts of composition, conditional use and information-based handling for a selected everyday acidic solution. Corrected case2 supplies the actual D rules; the image is an orienting example, not their complete assessment material.

The image does not cover every case1 substance, environmental case2 E, the unknown-composition F comparison or all protective conditions; those remain complete in supplied cases. No universal pH-based inference, advanced mechanism or practical indicator execution is introduced.
